analyst.summary: HPCL posted a record FY26 profit (Rs 17,175 cr standalone PAT, up 133%), but almost all of that came from unusually strong refining margins ($8.79/bbl for the year, spiking to $14.27/bbl in the Mar-2026 quarter) rather than from its core fuel-retailing business, which is actually running at a loss right now because pump prices have stayed frozen even as crude oil spiked after the Feb-2026 Middle-East escalation. The stock looks statistically cheap (about 4.7x trailing earnings) but that multiple is flattered by a profit level unlikely to repeat if refining margins normalize or if the government continues holding pump prices flat against costlier crude. A large new refinery (Rajasthan, ramping through FY27) is the genuine long-term positive. Net: hold, don't chase the cheap-looking multiple, and watch the marketing-margin/crude-price gap closely.
